description: Test whether α₄ = 0.8272 (fitted from n→p) generalises to higher β-decay Q-values.  Tested transitions: n→p, T→³He, ¹⁴C→¹⁴N, ⁶He→⁶Li, ⁴⁰K→⁴⁰Ca.  Finding: the naive formula structure (Σ_n + chirality + tail) is NOT universal in n — the symmetric baseline (Σ_n - 1) only matches single-nucleon transition (n=3).  For multi-nucleon, the right baseline is parent-vs-daughter NF DIFFERENCE, analogous to Δ(net) = h(h-2)/2.  α₄ may still be universal for the tail coefficient if applied to the right baseline structure.
